full_judgment:
Bhabani Prasad Singha J : On an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure a Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the proceedings of Special Case No. 10 of 2008 arising out of Metropolitan Special Case No. 154 of 2008 corresponding to ACC GR Case No. 22 of 2008 arising out of Shahbagh PS Case No. 53 dated 26-2-2008 under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, now pending in the Court of Special Judge, Court No. 2 Dhaka should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of this case are that for production management and maintenance of Barapukuria Coal mine Co. Ltd. (herein after referred to as BCMCL), international tender was called where 3 international companies, namely, (1) Shan-dong Ludi Company Ltd, (2) Suja Cool Mining Group and (3) CMC consortium submitted tenders. Among the tenders the bid of the Shandong Ludi was the lowest and the tender of CMC consortium was highest. In view of non-compliance of the terms of the contract between the Shandong Ludi Company and the BCMCL by the Shandong Ludi Company by way of submitting Performance Guarantee and Bank guarantee, the Chairman, Petro Bangla proposed for retender in respect of the matter to the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources. Said proposal of the Chairman. Petro Bangla was not accepted. As per the proposal of the Cabinet Purchase Committee, the then Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia approved the proposal to give work order to the CMC although the difference of bid between the Shandong Ludi and CMC was about Taka 1,58,71,26,343.22 crores. With ill-intention in a preplanned way in collussion with and abetting each other and in criminal breach of trust instead of giving decision for re-tender as per proposal of the Chairman, Petro Bangla violating PPR, 2003, the accused-persons killed time on the pretext of shortage of time and gave the work order to the CMC, the highest bidder causing a loss of about Taka 158 crores to the Government and misappropriated the aforesaid money and thereby committed  offence punishable under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and hence, the case. 

 3. On receipt of the First Information Report (FIR) of the case SI Md. Monirul Haque was entrusted with the charge of investigation of the case who after investigation submitted Final Report as mistake of fact and that subsequently, after further investigation Md. Abul Kashem Fakir, the Deputy Director, Anti-Corruption Commission was entrusted with the charge of investigation of the case who after investigation submitted charge-sheet No. 409 dated 5-10-2008 under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 against the accused-petitioner and others. After submission of the charge sheet the record of the case was transmitted to the Court of Metropolitan Senior Special Tribunal, Dhaka where the case was registered as Metropolitan Special Case No. 154 of 2008 and subsequently, it was transferred to the Court of Special Judge, Court No. 2, Dhaka and was renumbered as Special Case No. 10 of 2008. After cognizance was taken in the case, the present accused-petitioner moved this Court by filing the instant application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the proceedings of said Special Case No. 10 of 2008 whereon the instant Rule was issued. 

 4. Mr. Nurul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused-petitioner submits that the facts as disclosed in the FIR and in the charge-sheet are preposterous which do not disclose any offence against the accused-petitioners; that there was no sanction prior to lodging of the FIR and submission of the charge-sheet of the case; that there is no basis for making These accused petitioners accused-persons in this case Lastly, the learned Advocate prays for quashing the impugned proceedings against these accused-petitioners. 

 5. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate representing the Anti-Corruption Commission submits that the case so far as relates to these accused-petitioners is not preposterous inasmuch as the FIR and the Charge- Sheet of the case disclosed prima-facie involvement of the accused-petitioners in the alleged occurrence that the disputed question of facts cannot be decided in case a filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and that it can only, be decided at the time of trial on the basis of evidence to be adduced; that these accused-petitioners abated the alleged occurrence and that at their connivance the occurrence took place. The learned Advocate lastly prays for discharging the Rule. 

 7. Admittedly, the case was investigated firstly by the first investigating officer SI Md. Monirul Haque who after investigations submitted Final Report as mistake of fact and that subsequently after further investigation, the Deputy Director Md. Abul Kashem Fakir submitted charge-sheet under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 against the accused-petitioners and the other accused-Persons. It is alleged in the charge-sheet that as per pre-plan with ill-intention in collusion with the each other, the accused-persons by wasting time managed the work order in favour of CMC causing a loss to the tune of Taka 1,58,71,26,343/22 crores to the Government and misappropriated it. 

 8. The petitioners of this case admittedly were the public servants at the relevant time acted for approval of the work order in favour of CMC consortium ignoring the recommendation of the Chairman, Petro Bangla for re-tender which prima-facie suggests that for giving pecuniary benefit to other accused-persons, they did it at the cost of the national interest. This impugned case is with regard to criminal breach of trust, misconduct and abetment with regard to manipulation of tender process against the accused-persons. Criminal breach of trust misconduct, and abetment are the factual aspects of the case which can only be decided at the time of trial on the basis of the evidence to be adduced. The FIR and the charge-sheet of the case clearly disclose prima-facie case against the accused-petitioners. The case also attracts the section 5(1) (d) of the Prevention of the Anti-Corruption Act, 1947. In this case amongst others allegations of commission of the offence, commission of offence of abetment under section 109 of the Penal Code has also been brought against the accused-persons. The matter of abetment can only be decided at the time of trial of the case on the basis of the evidence (Reference: The case of Anti-Corruption Commission vs Mehedi Hasan reported in 67 DLR (AD) 137). 

 9. In this case the accused-petitioners challenged the property and legality of order as passed by the Anti-Corruption Commission for further investigation of the case. But sections 19 and 20 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 amply empowers the Anti-Corruption Commission to make further investigation into a case. The materials on record further shows that the previous Investigating Officer Md. Monirul Haque without collecting evidence as required by law recommended for discharge of the accused-persons on the basis of statements of the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. It is the settled principal of law that the prosecution is always at liberty to take out further investigation into a case. The Anti-Corruption Commission being a prosecutor has every right to pass an order for further investigation in a case as per the provision of sections 19 and 20 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004. Further, as per section 173(3B) of the Code of Criminal Procedure there can be further investigation even after submission of charge-sheet. As to the question as raised by the learned Advocate for the accused-petitioners to the effect that there was no sanction either for lodging the FIR and for submit-ting the charge-sheet the answer is given in the case of Anti-Corruption Commission vs Dr. Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290. In the said case our Apex Court held that there is no requirement for sanction for initiation of the proceeding and that sanction is required only case of filing the charge-sheet. In the aforesaid case our Apex Court held that Both the sub-section (1) and sub-section (2) of section 32 envisages only one sanction, not two. Sub-section (1) does not spell out or even envisage filing of any fresh sanction when the sanction to prosecute has already been filed along with the charge-sheet of the Investigating Officer". Here in this case, the charge-sheet shows that with the prior sanction or approval of the Anti-Corruption Commission, the Investigating Officer submitted charge-sheet. So, the submission of the learned Advocate with regard to filing of charge-sheet without prior sanction of the Anti-Corruption Commission has no lag to stand. It is the law that when the materials on record disclosed a prima-facie case against an accused the proceedings cannot be quashed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Here in this case after investigation prima-facie case having been made out against the accused-petitioners, charge-sheet was submitted. The plain reading of the FIR and the charge-sheet of the case disclosed that despite the proposal of the Chairman, Petro Bangla to call international retender for non submission of performance guarantee and bank guarantee by Shandong Ludi company, the work order was given to CMC causing a huge lose to the Government to the tune of about Taka 158 crores in which the instant accused-petitioners played the role of abettors. It is mentioned in the charge-sheet that the accused-petitioners abetted the offence. The mens rea of these accused-petitioners the allegation of abetting the evidence against them and the factual aspects of the case can only be decided at the time of trial of the case on the basis of the evidence to be adduced at the time of trial. In the case of Anti-Corruption Commission vs Mehedi Hassan reported in 67 DLR (AD) 137, our Apex Court held that if prima-facie allegation of abetment regarding manipulation of the tender for sale of the abandoned property is disclosed from the materials collected by the prosecution the prosecution should not be debarred from proving the allegations of abetment by adducing evidence which may be oral, documentary and circumstantial". Our Apex Court further held in the said case that "abetment is such an offence which can be inferred from the conduct of the accused and attending circumstances of the case which may be proved by oral, documentary and circumstantial evidence. Disputed questions of fact cannot be determined by the High Court Division by invoking its extra-ordinary jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. What is more, whether the allegations of abetment in manipulating the tender are true or false can only be resolved during the trial of the case. The admissibility, property or sufficiency of materials collected by the prosecution are matters of evidence". We are in respectful agreement with the aforesaid decision of our Apex Court. 

 10. From the discussion made here above, we find that there is a prima-facie case against the accused-petitioners; that there is sanction from the Anti-Corruption Commission before submitting the charge-sheet in the case; that the cognizance of the offence has been taken in the case; there is no abuse of the process of the Court in the alleged proceeding; that there arise no question of quashing the impugned proceeding; that the disputed questions of fact involved in the case can only be decided during trial of the case on the basis of the evidence to be adduced by the parties. 

 11. It is worth mentioning that challenging the proceedings of self-same Shahbagh PS Case No. 53 of 26-2-2008 under sections 406/409/ 109/419/420 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 some of the other accused-persons of this case filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 19327 of 2008, 19328 of 2008 and 20335 of 2008 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and that all of the cases were discharged by two benches of the High Court Division answering all the questions with regard to the legality and property of the aforesaid Shahbagh PS Case. 

 14. The learned Special Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka is hereby directed to proceed with the Special Case No. 10 of 2008 arising out of Metropolitan Special Case No. 154 of 2008 corresponding to ACC GR Case No. 22 of 2008 arising out of Shahbagh PS Case No. 53 dated 26-2-2008 under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 so far it relates to the accused-petitioner as per law.
